deadline.value: Priority deadline is January 5 for full consideration; notification April 15, closing May 1. Later applications are considered on space available.
deadline.quote: Priority deadline for your application to be fully considered: January 5th

gre_subject.value: Neither the subject nor the general GRE is required, and GRE scores are not considered.
gre_subject.quote: Note: the subject and general GRE scores are not required for applications to our graduate program

supervisor.value: Applicants list faculty of interest, and first-year students are expected to meet research group leaders; admission does not guarantee a particular adviser.
supervisor.quote: we expect first year students to meet with the leaders of the research groups that they are interested in joining

funding.value: Most students receive a teaching assistantship with a stipend and tuition waiver; the FAQ says the vast majority are supported by an assistantship.
funding.quote: Most students receive a teaching assistantship (TA) contingent on being admitted to our program.

also.quote: the vast majority of our graduate students are supported through a graduate research assistantship (GRA) or a graduate teaching assistantship (GTA)

entry_route.value: New graduates are accepted; the admission list asks for a bachelor's transcript and no master's degree is listed.
entry_route.quote: New graduates are accepted for Fall term only.

toefl_min.value: The department requires an overall TOEFL of 4.2 (new 1-6 scale) with a speaking score of 20.
toefl_min.quote: For TOEFL, the overall score must be 4.2 or higher with a speaking score of 20 or higher.

ielts_min.value: The department requires an overall IELTS of 6.5.
ielts_min.quote: For IELTS, the overall and speaking scores must be 6.5 or higher.

notes: Astrophysics and gravity are research areas of this PhD in Physics, so the astronomy field is listed here; no separate astronomy PhD was found. The department's $70 fee and no-waiver rule match the Graduate School.
